title: Ceebu Yapp, Beef and Rice with Eggs
author: chefgod (whats4eats)
desc: Stewing beef marinated in the roff, browned, simmered with tomato paste, then joined by vegetables and 8–10 hard-boiled eggs before the ceebu jen rice method.
longDesc: A variation on SEN052: 2 pounds of stewing beef marinate in the roff for at least an hour, brown and are set aside; onions and roff cook, tomato paste goes in, stock or water follows, and the beef returns without vegetables for a long simmer — the page prints the time as ‘1 to 1/2 hours’, an apparent misprint kept as printed. Vegetables and 8 to 10 shelled hard-boiled eggs follow for 45 minutes, and the rice finishes in the strained broth as in the fish version.
ingredients: The roff of SEN052: 1/4 cup parsley, 2 or 3 chiles, 2 or 3 garlic cloves
Onions, tomato paste, stock or water, vegetables and rice as in SEN052 — quantities as listed there
steps: Marinate the beef in the roff for at least 1 hour.
Brown the beef and set it aside. Brown the onions and the remaining roff, add the tomato paste, then the stock or water. Return the beef — without the vegetables.
Simmer the beef ‘1 to 1/2 hours’ as printed (probably 1 to 1 1/2 hours; judge by tenderness).
Add the vegetables and the hard-boiled eggs and simmer 45 minutes.
Continue with the rice method of SEN052: lift out the meat, eggs and vegetables, strain and measure the broth, cook the rice in it, and serve.
chefTips: The printed time ‘1 to 1/2 hours’ is a descending range, almost certainly a misprint; cook the beef until tender.
Add the eggs with the vegetables, not earlier, so they don’t go rubbery.
Marinating at least an hour is the page’s only prep rule for the beef.
commonMistakes: Taking ‘1 to 1/2’ literally and under-cooking the beef.
healthBenefits: Beef and eggs add protein and iron.
culturalNote: ‘Yapp’ is the Wolof word for meat, parallel to ‘jen’ for fish; the etymology of ‘yapp’ itself is not given in the sources used here.
sources: Source: whats4eats.com, ‘Ceebu yapp (beef with rice and vegetables)’, a variation printed under SEN052’s page. Byline ‘chefgod’ (pseudonym, flagged). TWO-PASS.

SUSPECTED MISPRINT, FLAGGED, DO NOT FIX: ‘Simmer the beef for 1 to 1/2 hours.’ — a descending range, almost certainly ‘1 to 1 1/2 hours’. Both passes reported it identically, so the misprint itself is two-pass.

The variation page gives only the beef, eggs and times; all other quantities are inherited from SEN052 and are not repeated here. Prep and cook times in this entry are estimates from the stage list (1 hour marinate counted as prep).
